correctness.rationale: A positive base-(-p) integer has odd digit length. The least with 2k+1 digits is (p^(2k)+p)/(p+1), obtained by maximizing the negative-place digits under a leading 1. For k=2 this exceeds both the published descent threshold B_p and 5(p-1)^2 (the latter difference is (p-1)(p-2)(p-3)+1). Successive lower bounds increase by (p-1)p^(2k)>2(p-1)^2 for k>=2, so all integers of at least five digits descend, independently of the cited descent theorem. At most three slots give the closed positive core [1,3(p-1)^2]; B_p has digits (p-1,p-1,p-1) and attains its upper bound after one step. Independent replay in /workspace/branches/audit_negative_core.py uses ordinary-radix expansion after translating the signed digit interval and complementing odd-place digits, and iterates the image of the whole core to stabilization (exactly the cyclic vertices in a finite functional graph). All directed cycles, witness bounds and twenty nearest-happy entries agree. Checking 2 through p^2 and -2 through -p suffices since both endpoints map to 1; successive iterates either hit 1 or repeat. The same independent replay includes p=2 through 10, directly confirming the first primitive period 17 is at -18 in increasing absolute value, unique there. Negative inputs are not periodic because the first image is nonnegative; 0 is outside the asserted positive census.

value.rationale: The object and the four recorded invariants are the same as in a published complete census. A contiguous continuation matters because it establishes a sharp first-base threshold, not merely a period-17 example. The full directed witness sets provide an exact baseline for questions about feasible periods, and the -19 nearest negative happy value -17 illustrates why one cannot just report the universal happy endpoint -p. No general result about larger bases or arbitrary periods is implied.
